figures.shows: (a) a two-layer QPNN Bell-state analyzer circuit: two interferometer meshes U separated by single-site nonlinearities, with the Bell-state truth table, coloured by photon-number probability; (b) 3D bar chart of the probability of each output state given each input Bell state; (c) line plot of success rate (y, 0 to 1) against the number of BSA operations in series (x, 1 to 10), one curve for linear optics (lowest) and one each for realistic QPNNs of 2 to 4 layers with phase shifts pi, pi/4 and pi/10; the 2-layer pi curve is highest and decays slowest; purple marker marks the network of (a).
figures.confirmed_by: In Fig. 1c, we observe that using state-of-the-art waveguide fabrication (as described in Sec. II) and a perfect (π) two-photon nonlinearity, 10 BSA nodes made from 2-layer QPNNs can be applied in series with a success rate of 72%.

figures.confirmed_by: When trained in situ, the QPNN learns to overcome these imperfections as is seen by the convergence toward loss-limited performance (see Sec. VI for more information on network training and the loss limit).

papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of quantum photonic neural networks (Bell-state analyzers and GHZ generators) with fabrication loss, imperfect couplers and weak Kerr nonlinearities, showing in situ training recovers most fidelity and that an optimal network size exists.

existing.note: The 0.891 unconditional fidelity is for a 6-layer network with a pi/10 effective nonlinearity, which the stored value leaves out (it says only sub-optimal). The abstract names pi/10 and the Discussion gives 6 layers and the loss-limited setting at 0.3 dB/cm. The 0.999999 conditional figure is the abstract's statement; the body states 0.999999 for state-of-the-art loss with ideal nonlinearity (3 to 7 layers), and 0.99999 (0.99996) for a ten-BSA sequence of 6-layer pi/10 networks.
existing.value: The authors report that, with a sub-optimal pi/10 effective Kerr nonlinearity, a network fabricated with current state-of-the-art processes can achieve an unconditional fidelity of 0.891, that increases to 0.999999 if success is preconditioned on the detection of a photon in each logical photonic qubit; in the Discussion they give 0.891 for a 6-layer network at loss-limited operation.

existing.note: The optimal size depends on loss and nonlinearity. papers.what_it_is: A theoretical model of credit-market competition in which ex-ante identical lenders choose screening precision and rates, showing that correlated (nested) screening errors produce a segmented hockey-stick rate schedule while independent errors give a smooth one, and analysing entry of new screening technologies and open banking.

existing.note: The nested result is a theorem under Definition 1 (a less-skilled lender makes every error a more-skilled one makes, plus some more). Proposition 2 gives at most three segments and Region III exists only if the non-selective profit condition is met. The independent-errors result is Proposition 1. The abstract's single market segment for independent errors is a description of a smoothly increasing, fully separating schedule in which each skill level has its own rate, and under independent information some bad borrowers are always excluded.
existing.value: In their model of credit-market competition, the authors show that with nested (correlated) screening errors, potentially from similar AI systems and overlapping financial-sector data, ex-ante identical lenders specialize across at most three market segments, generating a hockey-stick interest-rate schedule, while with independent errors lenders separate across smoothly increasing interest rates, which the abstract describes as a single market segment.
